name: Titanium.UI
description:
The UI module is responsible for native user-interface components and interaction inside
Titanium.  The goal of the UI module is to provide a native experience along with native
performance by compiling Javascript code into their native counterparts as part of the
build process.

#### Design

The UI module is broken down into 3 major area:

* **Views** - [Views](api:Titanium.UI.View) are containers that host visual elements such as
controls or other views.  Views can have their properties customized, such as their border color
and radius, can fire events such as swipe events or touches, and can optionally contain a
hierarchy or other views as children. In Titanium, most views are specialized to perform both a
visual function and set of interaction behaviors such as [Table View](api:Titanium.UI.TableView) or
[Coverflow View](api:Titanium.UI.iOS.CoverFlowView).  Views are always named with the suffix `View`.

* **Controls** - controls, or sometimes referred as widgets, are visual elements such as
[sliders](api:Titanium.UI.Slider),  [buttons](api:Titanium.UI.Button) and [switches](api:Titanium.UI.Switch).
They provide a visual element which has a defined behavior and typical have special
configuration and special events.  Controls themselves are views and also inherit a views
properties, functions and events.

* **Windows** - [Windows](api:Titanium.UI.Window) are typically top-level visual constructs that are
the main part of your interface. An application will always have at least one window and windows
can take different shapes and sizes, can have display and interaction properties such as
fullscreen or modal and can be customized, such as changing their opacity or background color.
Windows themselves are views and also inherit a views properties, functions and events. There
are a few specialization of Windows such as a [Tab Group](api:Titanium.UI.TabGroup) which offer
additional behavior beyond the basic Window. It is considered a best practice to use a
[NavigationWindow](api:Titanium.UI.NavigationWindow) as the root of your application.

Titanium uses the [Factory Pattern](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factory_method_pattern) for
constructing objects and a general naming pattern for APIs.  For example, to construct a
[Alert Dialog](api:Titanium.UI.AlertDialog), you call the method [Titanium.UI.createAlertDialog](api:Titanium.UI#createAlertDialog).
To create a [TextArea](api:Titanium.UI.TextArea), you call the method [Titanium.UI.createTextArea](api:Titanium.UI#createTextArea).
Once an object is created, it will be available until it goes out of scope.

#### Optimizations

UI objects are optimized by Titanium to not be realized into the drawing context and placed into
the device UI surface until needed.  That means that you can create UI objects, set their
properties and add them to their hierarchy without much worry about memory or performance.
When the native drawing surface needs to render a specific view or control, Titanium will
automatically create the view as needed.  Additionally, Titanium is optimized to also release
memory once the view is no longer needed, on screen or in low memory situations.  However, it's
a good idea to help Titanium along in certain cases where you are no longer using objects.  For
example, you should call `close` on a [Window](api:Titanium.UI.Window) instance when you are no
longer using it.  You can safely call `open` on the window again to re-open it.

#### Global Context

Prior to the release of Titanium SDK `9.0.0.GA` any variable declared in `app.js` or `alloy.js`
was added to a global scope. This however is no longer the case since `9.0.0.GA`. However
it is still possible to add variables to a global scope by adding `global.` in front of any
variable declared in `app.js` or `alloy.js`. However you should be careful with adding variables
to global context because anything added to the global context will not be garbage-collected.

In Alloy the recommended way to add global context is `Alloy.Globals`.

#### Portability

Titanium components are designed to be portable across as many platforms as it supports.
However, there are cases where a device either does not support a specific feature or capability
or where it support additional functionality. For cases where the device OS supports
capabilities that other platforms do not, we attempt to place those capabilities in a separate
namespace, such as [Titanium.UI.iOS](api:Titanium.UI.iOS). However, in cases where the control is in a common
namespace and support additional features, we continue to place that functionality directly on
the object.

#### Events

Event listeners must be defined before their respective events are likely to be fired, otherwise
they are not guaranteed to be called. The open and focus [Window](api:Titanium.UI.Window) event
listeners, for instance, must be defined before the window is opened.

Evaluating events as late as possible while bearing the above consideration in mind, however,
can significantly improve application responsiveness. For example, an event listener for a
click event may be defined after the parent window has been opened.

Adding `eventListeners` in Alloy makes sure they are bound before they are fired.

#### Colors

Many UI components have properties that control their color.

Colors may be specified as a hex triplet to determine the red, green and blue channels. Thus,
`'#000000'` is specified for black, `'#ff0000'` for red, `'#00ff00'` for green, `'#0000ff'` for
blue, and `'#ffffff'` for white, etc. A channel may be abbreviated when its two hex digits are
identical, such as `'#000'`, `'#f00'`, `'#0f0#'`, `'#00f'` and `'#fff'` for the above colors,
respectively.

An additional alpha channel is supported as a prefix to the hex triplet (ARGB or AARRGGBB). So, to make
the purple-like color `'#ff00ff'` semi-opaque, you could use an alpha value of `'55'`, giving,
`'#55ff00ff'` or `'#5f0f'`. Please note that both iOS and Android use ARGB format, while typical CSS supports RGBA.

Note that while the pound symbol, `#`, is not mandatory on iOS when using the hex triplet format,
it is recommended to include it to provide compatibility with other platforms.

iOS and Android also accept colors specified in the form, `rgb(R,G,B)` and `rgba(R,G,B,A)`, with the color
channels inside the parentheses represented by integer numbers between `0` and `255` and the
alpha channel by a float number between `0` and `1.0` (transparent to opaque, respectively).
For example, an opaque purple could be obtained using `'rgb(255,0,255)'` and a semi-opaque purple
using `'rgba(255,0,255,0.3)'`. Note that although this format will work if the `rgb` or `rgba`
prefix is omitted, this is not officially supported and thus not recommended.

Alternatively, the following set of color names are recognized.

`'aqua'`, `'black'`, `'blue'`, `'brown'`, `'cyan'`, `'darkgray'`, `'fuchsia'`, `'gray'`,
`'green'`, `'lightgray'`, `'lime'`, `'magenta'`, `'maroon'`, `'navy'`, `'olive'`, `'orange'`,
`'pink'`, `'purple'`, `'red'`, `'silver'`, `'teal'`, `'white'`, `'yellow'`.

All color properties also accept a value of `'transparent'`.

On Android, if you want to create a semi-transparent window, set the `opacity`
property **before** opening the window.

On iOS, you can set a global tinting using [Titanium.UI.tintColor](api:Titanium.UI#tintColor). All child views will inherit
the tint color by default and are able to override the color using `tintColor` on their own views.
The default `tintColor` on iOS is the blue (system-color).

If a color property is undefined, the default color of the particular UI element is applied.
If a color value is not valid on iOS, the default color is applied, whereas, on Android, the
color yellow is applied.

On iOS, you may use named system colors. See the [Titanium.UI.Color](api:Titanium.UI.Color) documentation for more details.

#### Dark Mode

In iOS 13 Apple introduced support for users to adopt a system-wide Dark Mode setting where the screens, view, menus, and controls use a darker color palette. You can read more about this in the Apple Human Interface Guidelines.

There are two aspects to dark mode that can be specified for your app, colors and images.

##### Specifying Dark Mode colors

To specify colors for dark mode, also known as semantic colors, first create a file called `semantic.colors.json` in the Resources directory for classic applications, or in the assets directory for Alloy applications. Then you can specify color names in the following format:

``` json
  {
    "textColor": { // the name for your color
      "dark": {
        "color": "#ff85e2", // hex color code to be set
        "alpha": "50" // can be set from a range of 0.0-100.0, integer or float
      },
      "light": "#ff1f1f" // can be a hex color (with alpha via ARGB/AARRGGBB)
    }
  }
```

To reference these colors in your application use the [Titanium.UI.fetchSemanticColor](api:Titanium.UI#fetchSemanticColor) API, this is a cross platform API that on iOS 13 and above will use the native method that checks the users system-wide setting, and in all other instances will check the [Titanium.UI.semanticColorType](api:Titanium.UI#semanticColorType) property and return the correct color for the current setting.

You may also directly use the named of the colors as values to any color properties on UI elements.

##### Specifying Dark Mode images

Note: Dark Mode images are iOS only.

To specify dark mode images, use the `-dark` suffix on the image name. When building your app the images are set as the dark mode variant, then refer to images as normal and iOS will select the correct image dependent on the users system-wide setting.

For example given an image `logo.png` with `@2x` and `@3x` variants, the following dark mode images should exist:

  * logo-dark.png
  * logo-dark@2x.png
  * logo-dark@3x.png

And you would reference the image as before using `logo-dark.png`

Android:
You can use the native `app/assets/android/images/res-night` folder (extend them with e.g. `res-night-xxhdpi` if needed) for dark-mode images.

properties.name: ANIMATION_CURVE_EASE_IN
properties.summary:
Use with [Animation.curve](api:Titanium.UI.Animation#curve) to specify an animation that starts
slowly and speeds up.

properties.name: ANIMATION_CURVE_EASE_IN_OUT
properties.summary:
Use with [Animation.curve](api:Titanium.UI.Animation#curve) to specify an animation that starts
slowly, and speeds up, then slows down at the end of the animation.

properties.name: ANIMATION_CURVE_EASE_OUT
properties.summary:
Use with [Animation.curve](api:Titanium.UI.Animation#curve) to specify an animation that starts
quickly, then slows down at the end of the animation.

properties.name: ANIMATION_CURVE_LINEAR
properties.summary:
Use with [Animation.curve](api:Titanium.UI.Animation#curve) to specify an animation that proceeds
at a constant rate.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_BACKGROUND_COLOR
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to specify a background color.
properties.description:
Use a color name or hex value for [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_BASELINE_OFFSET
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to apply a different baseline to the text.
properties.description:
Set [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to a number to specify how many pixels to raise or lower the text.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_EXPANSION
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to stretch the text horizontally.
properties.description:
Set [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to a float value to specify how much to stretch the text.

For iOS, the default value is 0.0 and has no minimum/maximum range specified.
For Windows, the default value is 0.0 and the valid range is between 0.5 and 1.0.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_FONT
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to specify a font.
properties.description:
Use a [Font](api:Font) dictionary for [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_FOREGROUND_COLOR
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to specify a font color.
properties.description:
Use a color name or hex value for [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_KERN
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to specify kerning (space between characters).
properties.description:
Set [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to a float value specifying how many pixels to increase the character
spacing.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_LETTERPRESS_STYLE
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to use a letterpress text effect.
properties.description:
Use this constant when [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) is
[Titanium.UI.ATTRIBUTE_TEXT_EFFECT](api:Titanium.UI#ATTRIBUTE_TEXT_EFFECT).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_LIGATURE
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to enable or disable ligatures.
properties.description:
Set [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to `1` to enable ligatures, else `0` to disable.
Ligatures are only supported on certain fonts.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to wrap and truncate the text.
properties.description:
Set [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to a `Titanium.UI.ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK_*` constant.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information on type modes.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK_BY_CHAR_WRAPPING
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to wrap words at word boundaries.
properties.description:
Use this constant when [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) is
[Titanium.UI.ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK](api:Titanium.UI#ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK_BY_CLIPPING
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to set lines to not draw past the edge of the text container.
properties.description:
Use this constant when [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) is
[Titanium.UI.ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK](api:Titanium.UI#ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK_BY_TRUNCATING_HEAD
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to use ellipsis glyph at the beginning of the line for missing text.
properties.description:
Use this constant when [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) is
[Titanium.UI.ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK](api:Titanium.UI#ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK_BY_TRUNCATING_MIDDLE
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to use ellipsis glyph at the middle of the line for missing text.
properties.description:
Use this constant when [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) is
[Titanium.UI.ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK](api:Titanium.UI#ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK_BY_TRUNCATING_TAIL
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to use ellipsis glyph at the end of the line for missing text.
properties.description:
Use this constant when [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) is
[Titanium.UI.ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK](api:Titanium.UI#ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK_BY_WORD_WRAPPING
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to wrap words at word boundaries.
properties.description:
Use this constant when [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) is
[Titanium.UI.ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK](api:Titanium.UI#ATTRIBUTE_LINE_BREAK).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_LINK
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to create a link.
properties.description:
Set [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to a URL.

Use the Label's [link](api:Titanium.UI.Label#link) event to determine when the user triggers a
long press (not a click) event on the linked text.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_OBLIQUENESS
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to skew the text.
properties.description:
Set [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to a float value to specify how much to skew the text.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_PARAGRAPH_STYLE
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to manages the behaviour of string set.
properties.description:
Use [ParagraphAttribute](api:ParagraphAttribute) for the 'value' property in the attribute dictionary.
Range for this should be whole string.
See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information on type modes.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_SHADOW
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to display a shadow behind the text.
properties.description:
Set [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to a [Shadow](api:shadowDict) dictionary.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_STRIKETHROUGH_COLOR
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to change the color of the horizontal line.
properties.description:
Use a color name or hex value for [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value).

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_STRIKETHROUGH_STYLE
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to place a horizontal line through the text.
properties.description:
Set the `value` property to a `Titanium.UI.ATTRIBUTE_UNDERLINE_*` constant.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_STROKE_COLOR
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to specify a color for the stroke text.
properties.description:
Use a color name or hex value for the `value` property in the attributes dictionary.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information on type modes.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_STROKE_WIDTH
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to specify the width of the stroke text.
properties.description:
Set [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to a float value specifying the size of stroke width as a percentage of the
font size. A positive value displays an outline of the character, while a negative value
fills the character.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_SUBSCRIPT_STYLE
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to place the text in a lower position.
properties.description: See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_SUPERSCRIPT_STYLE
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to place the text in an upper position.
properties.description: See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: ATTRIBUTE_TEXT_EFFECT
properties.summary: Use with [Attribute.type](api:Attribute#type) to apply a text effect.
properties.description:
Set [Attribute.value](api:Attribute#value) to `Titanium.UI.ATTRIBUTE_LETTERPRESS_STYLE` to apply a
letterpress effect to the text.

See [Attribute](api:Attribute) for more information.

properties.name: BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEGATIVE
properties.summary: Use with [Button.style](api:Titanium.UI.Button#style) to show a negative themed escape button.
properties.description:
This is a text-only button without a background. It is intended to be used in conjunction with
[BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_POSITIVE](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_POSITIVE) and
[BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEUTRAL](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEUTRAL) to show an
escape button to exit a window or dialog such as "Cancel", "No", etc.

This is not supported on iOS and will use [BUTTON_STYLE_TEXT](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_TEXT) instead.

On Android, this can be customized by the `buttonBarNegativeButtonStyle` attribute. By default,
Android's built-in themes will style this button the same as
[BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEUTRAL](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEUTRAL) and
[BUTTON_STYLE_TEXT](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_TEXT).

properties.name: BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEUTRAL
properties.summary: Use with [Button.style](api:Titanium.UI.Button#style) to show a normal themed option button.
properties.description:
This is a text-only button without a background. It is intended to be used in conjunction with
[BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_POSITIVE](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_POSITIVE) and
[BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEGATIVE](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEGATIVE) to show
a normal informational button.

This is not supported on iOS and will use [BUTTON_STYLE_TEXT](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_TEXT) instead.

On Android, this can be customized by the `buttonBarNeutralButtonStyle` attribute. By default,
Android's built-in themes will style this button the same as
[BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEGATIVE](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEGATIVE) and
[BUTTON_STYLE_TEXT](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_TEXT).

properties.name: BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_POSITIVE
properties.summary: Use with [Button.style](api:Titanium.UI.Button#style) to show a positive themed accept button.
properties.description:
This is a text-only button without a background. It is intended to be used in conjunction with
[BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEGATIVE](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEGATIVE) and
[BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEUTRAL](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_OPTION_NEUTRAL) to show an an accept button
before closing a window or dialog such as "OK", "Yes", "Done", etc. It is typically colored
differently than a [BUTTON_STYLE_TEXT](api:Titanium.UI#BUTTON_STYLE_TEXT) themed button on iOS.

On Android, this can be customized by the `buttonBarPositiveButtonStyle` attribute.

By default, the Android material theme does not style this button differently than any other
text-only button. Only the holo theme will style it differently.
